chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Khallad ibn Khalid, from al-Qasim ibn Ma'n, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the son of a brother and a grandfather, he said: 'The estate is divided between them into two halves.'
ai.seo_question: How is the inheritance divided between a grandfather and a paternal nephew according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes an equal division of the estate between the paternal nephew (ibn al-akh) and the grandfather (jadd), reflecting the Shia juristic view that the grandfather is treated as a primary heir comparable to the father in this specific configuration. This ruling highlights the Shia position that the grandfather does not exclude the nephew, distinguishing it from some Sunni schools where the grandfather may exclude the nephew or where the division differs based on the presence of other heirs. The hadith underscores the principle of *qurb* (proximity) in inheritance, where the grandfather's closeness to the deceased balances the nephew's claim through the paternal line.
